chapter: Ellington band members and life on the road
title: Cooking steaks in the baggage car and making Duke pay
summary: Living on the band's Pullman cars, Bigard and Billy Taylor cooked on a kerosene stove and soon had Duke buying the steaks while they cooked them.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: -- no troubles. Oh, we got smart. We had two Pullman's and a baggage car. So Billy Taylor and I, we got together and we bought one of those little kerosene stoves, you know, and whenever we got into -- whatever town we're going to play in -- well, we lived on those cars, you see. We lived on them. So if we wanted steaks or anything, we'd go out, buy our steaks and whatever we wanted -- if we wanted some potatoes or anything. So we start cooking in the baggage car. So Duke found that out. So Duke come back there while we was cooking. He smelled that. You know, he liked to eat, you know. He said, "Oh, boy, that smells good." He said, "Where'd you guys get that?" We said, "We bought it. Where do you think we got it?" He said, "You got an extra one?" We said, "No." He said, "Can you get an extra one?" "Sure, we can get another one." He said, "How much?" I said, "I don't know. What you want to pay for it?" He said, "I want a good thick one." We said, "Well, give me some thick money. We'll go out and get it."
So he gave us $10 and we went out and -- he said, "I want the same thing you guy's got." So we got the steak or potatoes or whatever and we give him his change back. We
just gave him -- what it cost us. We didn't rob him. So then he's trying to make it a habit now, you know. "What time you're going to cook?"
You cooked the steak (unintelligible) after he bought it or did you make him cook his own?

No, we cooked because he couldn't cook nothing. And sometimes we'd get chicken -- anything we felt like. And especially what come in handy after the job was over and we'd go to the station and get on our trains, go to the baggage car and do our own cooking. You see, now, that was great. So then we got so we said, "Well, now," -- I told Billy, I said, "Billy, we got to fix him for this." So Billy said, "What?" I said, "Tell him to buy the stuff. Let him buy it. We're cooking it."

So we got him like that. We made him buy the steaks or whatever we're going to do. "You buy it and we'll cook it and we'll give you some." So we got him like that, you see? Well, that paid for the stove and it paid for the gas, whatever. It paid for the food.

Well, then, everybody in the whole band wanted us to cook for them. We said, "No way."

Remember when he was here last -- Johnny Hodges was cooking chicken, remember, at that place near the union?
